items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 1:15PM PST until November 28 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 11
feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM PST
Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 7.7
feet will peak between 10 AM and 11 AM Friday morning.
items.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

items.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued November 26 at 12:20PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
items.description:
A large and long period westerly swell will produce a risk of
breaking waves in the Morro Bay and Ventura Harbor entrances
through this evening. These conditions have a history of capsizing
vessels of various sizes resulting in serious injury or death,
even to the most experienced mariners.

Mariners are urged to stay clear of these harbor entrances during
the time mentioned. For more information, contact the local
harbor patrol or coast guard station and continue to monitor NOAA
Weather Radio for the latest weather information.
